findings.body: The doc comment says "Shorten `text` to at most `limit` characters," and the module doc says the limit comes from GitHub and the finding schema. When `rfind(' ')` returns `None` (no space in the first `limit` characters — e.g. a long Japanese title), the function returns `head` (exactly `limit` chars) plus the ellipsis, giving `limit + 1` characters. The `Some` branch is fine because it drops at least the space before adding the ellipsis. A caller that trusts the documented bound and writes the result into a capped field would overflow by one character. The multibyte test acknowledges this with `<= 21` for `limit = 20`, but the contract says `limit`.
findings.title: Keep shorten output within limit when no word boundary is found

value.summary: The new `summarise` module adds `shorten` and `first_sentence` helpers. `shorten` is mostly sound — it correctly works in character boundaries and avoids the multibyte panic it was written to fix — but its no-space-found branch returns `limit + 1` characters, exceeding the documented ceiling of `limit`.
